RE-CON-005.explanation: Missouri's statute of frauds, RSMo 432.010, bars enforcing a contract for the sale of land unless it or a memorandum of it is in writing and signed by the party to be charged. A handshake does not satisfy it, so the buyer cannot force the sale.
RE-CON-005.question: An oral $250,000 house sale agreement is never signed, and the seller backs out. The agreement is:

RE-CON-006.explanation: RSMo 432.010 requires a lease for a longer time than one year to be in writing and signed by the party to be charged. A month-to-month or one-year lease can be oral.

RE-CON-026.explanation: In Missouri a licensee may act as a dual agent only with the consent of all parties, given in a written agreement entered before acting (RSMo 339.750.1, 339.780.4). Acting for more than one party without everyone's knowledge is grounds for discipline under RSMo 339.100.2(6).
RE-CON-026.question: To represent both her listing seller and her buyer client where law permits, an agent must first:

RE-CON-027.explanation: RSMo 339.820 lets a Missouri designated broker appoint affiliated licensees in writing as designated agents for each client, and the broker is not a dual agent solely because of the appointment. Subagency involves a cooperating licensee working for the seller through the listing broker.
RE-CON-027.question: A broker appoints different salespeople to represent the seller and the buyer in one sale. This is:

RE-CON-028.question: In Missouri, a licensee who helps both buyer and seller complete a sale without representing either as an advocate is a:
RE-CON-028.explanation: RSMo 339.710(23) and 339.755 define the Missouri transaction broker as a licensee who assists the parties without an agency or fiduciary relationship. A dual agent does represent both parties, with their written consent.

RE-CON-029.explanation: Under RSMo 339.780.5, when a listing broker has made a unilateral offer of subagency, a cooperating broker becomes a subagent by disclosing that status to the customer. The subagent owes its duties to the seller, so the buyer is a customer (RSMo 339.710(10)).
RE-CON-029.question: To a cooperating agent acting as the seller's subagent through the MLS, an unrepresented buyer is:

RE-CON-035.explanation: RSMo 339.730.2 bars a seller's agent from disclosing confidential information about the client, and a seller's willingness to accept less is protected even in dual agency (RSMo 339.750.4(2)). It is not an adverse material fact about the property.
RE-CON-035.question: Asked for the seller's lowest price, which is $20,000 below list, the listing agent should:

RE-CON-037.explanation: A Missouri seller's agent must disclose to customers all adverse material facts actually known or that should have been known (RSMo 339.730.3), and concealing material facts is grounds for discipline (RSMo 339.100.2(2)). Waiting for a buyer to ask is not enough.
RE-CON-037.question: A seller asks the agent to hide unseen basement flooding in heavy rain. The agent should:

RE-CON-039.explanation: Under RSMo 339.730.3 a Missouri seller's agent owes a customer no duty except disclosure of all adverse material facts actually known or that should have been known, and honest dealing is required by RSMo 339.100.2(2). Loyalty and the other agency duties belong only to the client.

RE-DISC-018.explanation: A stigmatized property carries a psychological impact from an event, not a physical flaw. In Missouri, RSMo 442.600 calls this psychologically impacted real property, says it is not a material fact that must be disclosed, and bars suits against licensees for not disclosing it.
RE-DISC-018.question: A defect-free home where a homicide occurred years ago is best described as:

RE-FIN-013.explanation: RESPA Section 8 bans fees, kickbacks or anything of value given for referring settlement service business, and 20 CSR 2250-8.110(5) requires Missouri licensees to comply with RESPA. Disclosure does not make a referral fee legal; only bona fide payment for services actually performed is allowed.
RE-FIN-013.question: A title company offers a salesperson $200 per referred buyer. Under RESPA, accepting it is:

RE-PRAC-001.explanation: Drafting custom legal language is the unauthorized practice of law. 20 CSR 2250-8.140 lets a Missouri broker only fill in blanks on approved standard forms, and 20 CSR 2250-8.110(3) bars discouraging the use of an attorney.
RE-PRAC-001.question: A seller wants the salesperson to draft a custom life estate clause. The salesperson should:

RE-PRAC-002.explanation: 20 CSR 2250-8.120(2) requires a Missouri licensee to deliver immediately to the broker all money received in a transaction, and the broker deposits it in escrow within ten banking days after the last signature (8.120(1)). Handing it to the seller or holding it personally breaches the duty to account.
RE-PRAC-002.question: A salesperson receives a buyer's earnest money check with an offer on Friday. The salesperson should:

RE-PRAC-003.explanation: Mixing client money with the broker's own funds is commingling. RSMo 339.105.1 requires a separate escrow or trust account and allows personal funds in it only to cover service charges.

RE-PRAC-005.explanation: 20 CSR 2250-8.020(1) makes Missouri brokers responsible for supervising the real estate activities of all licensed and unlicensed persons associated with them. Independent contractor status, which RSMo 339.010.2 allows, does not remove that duty.
